newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wages data setback to inflation - RBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wages data setback to inflation - RBA.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday recent data on wages growth had been a setback to prospects for improving inflation.

Speaking on monetary policy, growth and unemployment to the Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce Macfarlane said it was an assessment of improving prospects for inflation, and the associated scope for additional growth, that lay behind the three easings in policy in the second half of last year.
"We would like to have seen that pattern of news continue, but the latest data on wages seems to have been a setback to that expectation," he said.

Macfarlane said the process was very similar to that followed by the Federal Reserve in the U.S. He noted an example of policy in action during 1996 when strong U.S. economic growth led markets to expect a tightening which never came.
This was because the Fed had continued to receive feedback on the economy indicating rises in prices and wages remained moderate and so it was able to allow growth to run longer.

"No-one would be more pleased than the Reserve Bank to see a similar outcome for the Australian economy over the next 12 or 18 months - that is continuing good news on wages and prices allowing us to grow faster for longer," he said.
This was why the recent wages data were a setback to the bank's expectations.
The latest figures on average weekly ordinary time earnings for full-time employees showed stronger than expected growth of 1.3 percent in the three months to February.
That took annual wages growth to 4.6 percent from 3.9 percent the quarter before and into the 4.5-5.0 percent zone which the RBA has expressed concerns about in the past.
